newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up, led by Lujiazui.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up, led by Lujiazui.

text.p: Shanghai B shares reversed morning losses to end up on Friday, led by gains in Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development due to institutional support buying, brokers said.
The B index rose 2.125 points or 2.58 percent to 84.517 points on volume of 67.4 million shares worth $35.762 million, compared with $29.10 million on Thursday.
The decision of Lujiazui not to propose any dividend or bonus share issue dampened its price early in the afternoon, but support buying from a major institution later pushed it up, brokers said.
Shanghai Lujiazui rose $0.050 or 4.23 percent to $1.230 on volume of 4.1 million shares.
"Some institutions do not want to let Pudong shares fall so close to its seventh anniversary," one broker said, referring to the announcement of Pudong as a new development zone in 1990.
"Institutional support sparked follow-up buying, and that pushed the index up," he said.
"If there is no negative news at the weekend, the index will test 87 points early next week," another broker said.
Of 43 B shares, 42 traded, with 30 up, seven flat and five down.
Shanghai Friendship and Overseas Chinese was the star on institutional buying, surging $0.050 or 10.08 percent to $0.546 on volume of 4.9 million shares.

Shanghai Diesel Engine bucked the market trend and was the most actively traded stock on institutional unwinding-selling with investors concerned about its results. It slipped $0.004 or $0.508 on volume of 5.2 million shares.
The Shanghai A share index reversed early losses on speculative buying late in the session, brokers said.
The index rose 14.818 points or 1.07 percent to 1,399.606 points on volume of 787.1 million shares worth 9.6 billion yuan.
The SSE30 index gained 24.473 points or 0.69 percent to 3,596.287 points.
Qinhuangdao Yaohua Glass was the biggest gainer on institutional buying, up 0.85 yuan or 10.05 percent to 9.30 yuan on volume of 6.3 million shares.
